lesson_title: The Law of Supply: Why Bakers Bake More
hook_text: Pay a baker R4 a muffin and you get 30. Pay R20 and you get 200. Here is why.
clip_script: At R4 a muffin, hardly any baker bothers: 30 muffins. At R12, baking is worth it: 120. At R20, bakers work through the night and the neighbour starts baking too: 200. Price up, quantity supplied up. That is the law of supply. Why? More profit per muffin. Making extra costs more, overtime, extra electricity, flour bought in a hurry, so bakers only do it if the price pays. And a high price pulls in new bakers. Plot it and you get a ladder climbing from bottom left to top right. Buyers want low prices; sellers want high prices. Opposite directions. Now the jump. If flour suddenly costs more, bakers make fewer muffins at every price, and the whole ladder jumps left. A faster oven? It jumps right. Own price: climb the ladder. Anything else: move the ladder.
visual_style: A bakery at night with trays multiplying as a price tag rises; dots forming an upward ladder on a graph; the whole curve sliding left as a flour bag price tag spikes.
pacing: Quick price steps, a steady ladder build, a sharp jump at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the supply curve next to your demand curve.
